issues.quote: Monnier had made us all show our watches, as he does every year, and told me my case wanted cleaning
issues.fact: The fact sheet gives no information about whether Girard's watch was checked against others, synchronized, or accurate.
issues.misreading: A solver could take the dinner watch-comparison as implying Girard's watch was verified or set to the other watches, and so treat its readings as more reliable than the sheet supports. This is a hint about clock accuracy that the sheet does not give.

issues.quote: What did I take them for? A repeater, I would have said. In my trade you know the sound.
issues.fact: The fact sheet says only that Girard heard faint quick bells from the master's window. It does not say he identified them as a repeater.
issues.misreading: A solver could read this as Girard confirming that the bells were a repeater watch chiming, which adds an identification and a source the sheet does not give. This is awkward rather than a change to any reading.
